purpose: VibeVoice-ASR 9B comparative WER at a sample size with a usable confidence interval: torch-GPU bf16 reference vs hipEngine dense bf16 vs hipEngine Q4_K_M, 200 LibriSpeech test-clean clips
hardware: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ PRO 395, Radeon 8060S (gfx1151), 256-bit LPDDR5X, 133 GB unified

protocol.clips: 200 LibriSpeech test-clean utterances, round-robin across all 40 speakers and their chapters, 1744.4 s of audio
protocol.systems: torch-GPU bf16 (transformers reference), hipEngine dense bf16 (hipBLASLt prefill), hipEngine Q4_K_M (raw-block WMMA prefill + pack8 decode)
protocol.scoring: Whisper EnglishTextNormalizer + jiwer, micro-average (total errors / total reference words), greedy decoding in every lane, identical 24 kHz PCM per clip
protocol.isolation: one subprocess per lane; the HIP lanes assert torch was never imported
protocol.caveat: a fixed 200-clip subset, not the full 2620-utterance test-clean, so absolute WER differs from the published row by subset variance

significance.method: paired per-clip WER over the 200 clips both hipEngine lanes scored, 20000-sample bootstrap
significance.conclusion: Q4_K_M is statistically indistinguishable from dense bf16 at 200 clips; the paired interval includes zero and 190/200 clips are bit-identical in WER.

schema_compliance.note: the strict evaluator refuses to score a transcript that violates the engine's schema, and reports it per lane instead of aborting the run
